value.body: The Technical Graduate Course (TGC) is the Indian Army's permanent-commission entry for engineering graduates. Selected candidates train for about a year at the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun and are commissioned as Lieutenants, usually into technical arms such as the Corps of Engineers, Signals or EME. Courses start twice a year.

items.label: Stipend during training
items.note: Equal to the start of Pay Level 10

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Unmarried men with a B.E./B.Tech in a notified stream, or in the final year. Applications on the Join Indian Army website are shortlisted on engineering marks; shortlisted candidates attend a five-day SSB interview and a medical exam. Women engineers apply through the separate SSC (Tech) entry.

value.title: At a glance
items: No written exam — the cut-off is set by engineering percentage, then SSB performance decides merit.
Seats are few per course and divided across engineering branches.
It is a permanent commission, so it is a long-term career rather than a fixed term.
Military life means transfers, field postings and physical standards.

value.title: TGC-141 vacancies by engineering stream
value.note: One course's split of 30 vacancies; stream-wise numbers change from course to course.
